verses.text: Back when the judges led Israel, a famine hit the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live in Moab with his wife and their two sons.
His name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and their sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They arrived in Moab and settled there.
Then Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with her two sons.
The sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
Then Mahlon and Chilion both died. Naomi had lost her two sons as well as her husband.
Naomi got ready to return from Moab with her daughters-in-law. While in Moab she'd heard that the LORD had come to his people's aid and given them food.
She left the place where she'd been living, and the two women went with her. They set out on the road back to Judah.
Naomi told them, “Go back, each of you to your mother's home. May the LORD show you the same kindness you've shown to me and to those who died.
May the LORD give each of you a place of rest in the home of a new husband.” Then she kissed them, and they cried out and wept.
They said, “No. We're going back with you to your people.”
Naomi answered, “Go back, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I have any sons left to bear who could become your husbands?
Go back, my daughters. Go on your way. I'm too old to marry again. Even if I thought there was still hope and married tonight and had sons,
would you wait for them to grow up? Would you stay single that long? No, my daughters. I'm deeply grieved for you because the LORD's hand has turned against me.”
They wept loudly again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
Naomi said, “See, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her god. Go back with her.”
Ruth said, “Don't ask me to leave you or turn back from following you. Wherever you go, I'll go, and wherever you stay, I'll stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
Where you die, I'll die, and there I'll be buried. May the LORD deal with me as severely as he sees fit if anything but death separates us.”
When Naomi saw how determined Ruth was to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her.
So the two went on until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was stirred up. The people asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
She told them, “Don't call me Naomi. Call me Mara, because the Almighty has made my life bitter.
I left full, and the LORD brought me home empty. Why call me Naomi when the LORD has testified against me and the Almighty has brought suffering on me?”
So Naomi came back from Moab with Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law. They arrived in Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.
Naomi had a relative on her husband's side named Boaz. He was a wealthy man from Elimelech's family.
Ruth, the Moabite, told Naomi, “Let me go into the fields and gather leftover grain behind anyone willing to let me.” Naomi said, “Go ahead, my daughter.”
So Ruth went out and gathered grain behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to a field belonging to Boaz, who was from Elimelech's family.
Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, “May the LORD be with you.” They answered, “May the LORD bless you.”
Boaz asked the servant in charge of the harvesters, “Whose family is that young woman from?”
The servant answered, “She's the Moabite woman who came back from Moab with Naomi.
She asked, ‘May I gather grain behind the harvesters, among the bundles?’ She came this morning and has been working until now, apart from a short rest in the shelter.”
Boaz told Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Don't go to another field to gather grain. Stay here, close to the women who work for me.
Keep an eye on the field they're harvesting and follow them. I've told the young men to leave you alone. When you're thirsty, go to the jars and drink the water they've drawn.”
Ruth bowed with her face to the ground and asked, “Why have you been so kind and taken notice of me, even though I'm a foreigner?”

Boaz answered, “I've heard all about what you've done for your mother-in-law since your husband died. You left your father and mother and the land where you were born to come live among people you'd never known.
May the LORD repay you for what you've done. May you receive a full reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you've come for shelter.”
Ruth said, “May I keep finding favor with you, sir. You've comforted me and spoken kindly to me, even though I'm not one of your servants.”
At mealtime Boaz told her, “Come have some bread and dip it in the vinegar.” She sat beside the harvesters, and they passed her roasted grain. She ate until she was full and had some left over.
When she got up to gather more grain, Boaz told his young men, “Let her gather even among the bundles. Don't embarrass her.
Pull some stalks out of the bundles for her and leave them behind. Let her gather them without scolding her.”
Ruth gathered grain in the field until evening. When she beat out what she'd gathered, she had about an ephah of barley.
She carried it into town, where Naomi saw how much she'd gathered. Ruth also brought out the food she had left from the meal and gave it to her.
Naomi asked, “Where did you gather grain today? Where did you work? Bless the man who noticed you!” Ruth told her mother-in-law who she'd worked with. “The man I worked with today is named Boaz.”

Naomi said, “May the LORD bless him! The LORD hasn't stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead.” Then she told Ruth, “That man is a close relative of ours, one of the family members who can redeem what we've lost.”
Ruth the Moabite added, “He even told me to stay close to his workers until they've finished his whole harvest.”
Naomi told her daughter-in-law, “It's good for you to go out with his women workers, my daughter. In another field someone might hurt you.”
So Ruth stayed close to Boaz's women workers and gathered grain through the end of the barley and wheat harvests. She kept living with her mother-in-law.
Naomi told her daughter-in-law, “My daughter, shouldn't I find you a home where you can settle and be well cared for?
Boaz is our relative, isn't he? You've been working with his women. Tonight he'll be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
Wash, put on some oil, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor. Don't let him know you're there until he's finished eating and drinking.
When he lies down, notice where he's lying. Then go over, uncover his feet, and lie down. He'll tell you what to do.”
Ruth said, “I'll do everything you've told me.”
She went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.
After Boaz ate and drank and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the grain pile. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
Around midnight Boaz woke with a start and turned over. There was a woman lying at his feet.
He asked, “Who are you?” She answered, “I'm Ruth, your servant. Spread the corner of your cloak over me, because you're a close relative with the right to redeem our family.”
He said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You've shown even more kindness now than you did before by choosing to stay with the family instead of going after younger men, rich or poor.
Don't be afraid, my daughter. I'll do everything you've asked. Everyone in town knows you're a woman of character.
It's true that I'm a close relative, but there's someone more closely related than I am.
Stay tonight. In the morning, if he wants to act as your family redeemer, good. Let him do it. If he won't, then as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Lie down until morning.”
She lay at his feet until morning, then got up while it was still too dark to recognize anyone. Boaz had said, “Don't let anyone know a woman came to the threshing floor.”
He told her, “Hold out the cloak you're wearing.” She held it out, and he measured six portions of barley into it and put it on her. Then he went into town.
When Ruth got back to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, “How did it go, my daughter?” Ruth told her everything Boaz had done for her.
She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley and said, ‘Don't go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
Naomi said, “Wait here, my daughter, until you see how things turn out. He won't rest until he's settled it today.”
Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down. Just then the close relative he'd spoken about came by. Boaz said, “Come sit here, my friend.” So the man came over and sat down.
Boaz gathered ten elders of the town and asked them to sit there with them. They sat down.
Boaz told the close relative, “Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the piece of land that belonged to our relative Elimelech.

I thought you should hear about it first. Buy it in front of the people sitting here and the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, go ahead. If you don't, tell me so I know. You have the first right, and I'm next.” The man said, “I'll redeem it.”
Then Boaz said, “When you buy the field from Naomi, you also acquire it from Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the man who died, to carry on his name through his inheritance.”
The relative replied, “I can't redeem it myself without risking my own inheritance. You take my right to redeem it, because I can't.”
In earlier times in Israel, when people confirmed a redemption or exchange, one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other. That's how they made a transaction official.
The close relative told Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” and took off his sandal.
Boaz said to the elders and everyone there, “You're witnesses today that I've bought from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech, Chilion, and Mahlon.
I've also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, to carry on Mahlon's name through his inheritance so his name won't disappear from his family or his town. You're witnesses today.”

Everyone at the gate, including the elders, answered, “We're witnesses. May the LORD make the woman coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and become well known in Bethlehem.
Through the children the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your family become like the family of Perez, the son Tamar bore to Judah.”
Boaz took Ruth as his wife and slept with her. The LORD enabled her to become pregnant, and she gave birth to a son.
The women said to Naomi, “Praise the LORD! He hasn't left you without a family redeemer today. May the boy's name become well known in Israel.
He'll bring your life back to you and care for you in your old age. Your daughter-in-law, who loves you and has been better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.”
Naomi took the child into her arms and cared for him.
The women who lived near her said, “Naomi has a son!” They named him Obed. He became the father of Jesse, who became the father of David.
Here's the family line of Perez. Perez was the father of Hezron.
Hezron was the father of Ram, and Ram was the father of Amminadab.
Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
Salmon was the father of Boaz, and Boaz was the father of Obed.
Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David.
